Implemented upstream commit 24ada7fe (#1559) with matching changes to two files:

**`command.go`** — reordered `ExecuteC`: `InitDefaultCompletionCmd(args...)` and `checkCommandGroups()` now run *after* `initCompleteCmd(args)`, so the real argv is available when deciding whether to register the `completion` command.

**`completions.go`** — `InitDefaultCompletionCmd` now takes `args ...string` and no longer bails on `!HasSubCommands()`. Instead it counts "real" sub-commands (excluding `__complete` and `help`), and when there are none, it adds `completion` then immediately removes it unless `Find(args)` shows the command is being invoked directly (`prog completion ...`) or completed (`prog __complete completion ''`). This keeps single-command programs able to accept positional args.

Verification:
- `go test ./... -run 'TestInitDefaultCompletionCmd' -count=1` — all 7 subtests pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` — full suite green, no regressions

The change is shell-agnostic (command registration, not generated script output), so the bash/zsh/fish/powershell generators stay in sync automatically.
